# Cryptnox Product Documentation

> Official technical documentation for Cryptnox SA (Carouge, Geneva,
> Switzerland) — NFC smart cards for hardware wallets, FIDO2 authentication and
> PIV identity, plus SDKs, CLI tools and hardware reference material.
> Main website: https://www.cryptnox.com — Shop: https://shop.cryptnox.com
> Source code: https://github.com/cryptnox

Cryptnox security devices are smart cards: the hardware wallet, FIDO2 and PIV
products are ISO/IEC 7816 contact and ISO/IEC 14443 contactless (NFC) cards.
Cryptnox also sells USB smart card readers (USB-A, USB-C CCID and
NFC/contactless models) for using the cards with a computer — see
https://shop.cryptnox.com. The hardware wallet card also carries the FIDO
Alliance certified FIDO2 and U2F applets (FIDO2 CTAP2.1, Level 1), so it
doubles as a FIDO2 security key.

## FIDO2 card compatibility by service and platform

- [FIDO2 Card Compatibility — Services and Platforms](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-readers/fido2-compatibility.html): which online services and operating systems work with a Cryptnox FIDO2 NFC security key card, as second-factor or passwordless sign-in. Two composing tables: PLATFORM (Windows full CTAP2; iOS NFC CTAP2; Android CTAP1/U2F ONLY over external NFC keys; macOS varies; Linux needs the open-source Cryptnox FIDO2 HID bridge) and SERVICE (Microsoft Entra ID, Google, AGOV, SwissID, login.gov, Apple, GitLab, Facebook, X, Cloudflare, Shopify, Binance, Coinbase, Bitfinex, Bank of America, Dropbox, NordVPN, Fastmail, GoDaddy, SSH). Explains why Microsoft over Android NFC fails even though card and service are both CTAP2-capable, why one card can register twice, and that these cards are MFA-first with PIN-based user verification, not fingerprint

## Click-to-Tap: FIDO2 user presence on a desktop reader

- [Click-to-Tap — FIDO2 User Presence on a Desktop Reader](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-readers/click-to-tap.html): FIDO2/WebAuthn requires a user-presence check on every authentication. A USB security key has a touch button; a smart card in an ordinary contact reader has none, so the card must normally be pulled out of the slot and reinserted once per sign-in. The Cryptnox Click-to-Tap button drives a controlled extraction-and-reinsertion sequence at the protocol level, with no mechanical movement, so the card stays seated. Requires Cryptnox FIDO2 smart cards and Windows; on macOS and Linux the button has no effect and the device remains a standard CCID/PC-SC reader. Covers usage steps, troubleshooting (button does nothing, service never prompts, card not detected, FIDO2 on Linux needing the open-source Cryptnox FIDO2 HID bridge), and what Click-to-Tap is NOT: not a PIN replacement, not a security boundary, not a secure element, not applicable to eID/PIV/CAC cards. Protected by Austrian utility model GM 55114/2025, German utility model No. 202025108028.1 and US patent application No. 19/534.472 (pending)

## Smart card reader compatibility by country

- [Smart Card Reader Compatibility by Country](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-readers/reader-compatibility.html): which national eID and professional smart cards work with Cryptnox USB contact and contactless readers, country by country, with the official government middleware required for each. Covers Belgium (Belgian eID), Czechia (eObcanka), Estonia (ID-kaart), Germany (Fahrerkarte, Personalausweis/AusweisApp), Hungary, Italy (TS-CNS, CIE), Latvia, Luxembourg, Netherlands (UZI-pas/SafeSign), Poland (e-dowod), Portugal (Cartao de Cidadao), Romania, Slovakia, Spain (DNIe), Sweden (SITHS), Finland (FINeID), UK/Ireland (tachograph, NHS Smartcard), UAE (Emirates ID), US/Canada (CAC/PIV), and ICAO 9303 travel documents. States explicitly what the readers cannot do: 125 kHz cards, iPhone/iPad, on-device PIN entry, and PIV/CAC login over contactless

## Blockchain address control attestation (proof a wallet address is yours)

- [Blockchain Address Control Attestation](https://docs.cryptnox.com/address-control-attestation.html): technical reference for the sealed PDF certificate produced by Cryptnox Wallet identity verification, which evidences that an identified person demonstrated CRYPTOGRAPHIC CONTROL of one named blockchain public key or address by signing a Cryptnox challenge with the corresponding private key at a recorded time. Covers the production flow (identity document capture, optional ICAO 9303 ePassport NFC chip read, selfie/active liveness check, key selection across Bitcoin SegWit / Ethereum / TRON / XRP, on-card signature in an EAL6+ secure element), a field-by-field definition of the certificate (Issue Date, Name, Date of Birth, Passport Number, Issuing Country, Selfie Verification, ICAO NFC Chip, Public Key/Address in Hex/Bech32/Base58, Cryptnox Card Serial, Card Authenticity Check mapping to the SDK Origin state, Key Origin mapping to the SDK SeedSource state, Private Key Exposure), a six-step verification procedure for relying parties, and the electronic seal (issued by SSL.com; NOT a qualified electronic signature or seal). Maps the method to EBA/GL/2024/11 paragraph 83 method (d) — digitally signing a specific message — as distinct from method (c), the Satoshi test, under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Article 14(5) for self-hosted address transfers above EUR 1,000 from 30 December 2024. States explicitly what the attestation does NOT certify: legal ownership, continued control after the recorded time, asset balance, source of funds, AML/sanctions/tax status, contract consent, or any regulated financial service; and that Cryptnox SA does not retain identity documents, selfie/liveness images or biometric templates after issuance

## Open-source crypto payment terminal (cryptnox-pos, ESP32 dev kit)

- [Cryptnox POS: Open-Source Crypto Payment Terminal (ESP32 Dev Kit)](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-pos.html): guide to cryptnox-pos, the open-source LGPL-3.0 firmware that turns an ESP32-2432S028 "Cheap Yellow Display" (ESP32-WROOM-32, ILI9341 240x320 touchscreen) plus a PN532 NFC module over I2C into a tap-to-pay crypto payment terminal. The customer taps a Cryptnox Hardware Wallet card (firmware v1.6.0 or later), the card signs the EIP-1559 transfer inside its EAL6+ secure element after PIN verification, the terminal broadcasts it over JSON-RPC and shows Approved only on a mined receipt. Accepts ETH, USDC and USDT on Ethereum (Sepolia test network), POL, USDC and USDT on Polygon (Amoy), TRX and USDT on Tron (Nile; USDC on Tron test-only). Covers the parts list, wiring (PN532 SDA to GPIO 27, SCL to GPIO 22, switches 1 0), flashing the prebuilt release image with esptool or the browser flasher, building from source with ESP-IDF v5.5, first-time setup through the terminal's own Wi-Fi access point and QR code (admin code and payout addresses confirmed on the panel, addresses read off a Cryptnox card), the payment flow, firmware updates over Wi-Fi carried by a browser, the optional secure build (Flash Encryption, encrypted NVS, Secure Boot v2 with irreversible eFuses), troubleshooting and FAQ. States plainly that it is a reference/educational dev kit, not a tamper-resistant terminal (card PIN and Wi-Fi password in plaintext RAM at run time), that private keys never leave the card, and that it is not the issuer-run C-WaaS terminal
- [Cryptnox POS: first-time setup](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-pos-setup.html): step by step with screenshots: admin code typed on the terminal only, joining the terminal's own Wi-Fi (Cryptnox-XXXX) by QR code, the setup page at 192.168.4.1, authorising the browser by matching a four-digit browser number on both screens, reading the merchant's payout addresses off their Cryptnox card (PIN on the terminal, Ethereum/Polygon and Tron addresses each accepted on the terminal screen) or typing them, joining the shop Wi-Fi, Configuration complete
- [Cryptnox POS: take a USDC payment](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-pos-payment.html): the merchant picks network and coin (Ethereum, USDC ERC-20) and types the amount, the customer reviews total, recipient, maximum network fee and token contract, enters the card PIN, taps the Cryptnox Hardware Wallet card, the terminal checks the balance and the card signs, Approved with a shortened transaction hash once mined
- [Cryptnox POS: settings and the control panel](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-pos-settings.html): swipe the bottom bar of the sale screen up, admin code, the four tabs Screen (brightness, touch calibration), Wi-Fi, Tx (asset, contract, Send to payout address, max and priority gas fees in Gwei, read-only) and About (version, Update, Reset); the phone settings page sections Network (Production or Test, terminal restarts), Token contracts, Gas fees, Clock time zone, Payout addresses, Wi-Fi, Firmware (signed .bin via Browse, not from the captive sign-in window); 15-minute session, Done to close
- [cryptnox-pos firmware reference (Doxygen)](https://docs.cryptnox.com/cryptnox-pos/): generated documentation for the firmware, with the config-portal, over-the-air update and security-analysis documents
- [cryptnox-pos on GitHub](https://github.com/cryptnox/cryptnox-pos): source code and release binaries
